d: (a figurative extension of meaning of θριαμβεύω ‘to lead prisoners of war in a victory procession,’ not occurring in the NT) to demonstrate one’s successful conquest of opposition
to gain complete victory over, as the result of a strenuous struggle
to subject someone or something to a superior force
to prevail over something or some person so as to be able to defeat, with the implication that the successful participant has greater strength
(a figurative extension of meaning of {L:πατέω<SDBG:πατέω:000001>}[b] ‘to trample,’ {D:19.51}) to conquer and keep under subjection
(a figurative extension of meaning of {L:συντρίβω<SDBG:συντρίβω:000001>}[b] ‘to crush,’ {D:19.46}) to overcome, with the resulting crushing of the power of the opposition
to be completely and overwhelmingly victorious
